messages:
Dara (FinOps): MeterMate renewal landed, but INV-2026-0520 shows a ~12% higher usage charge vs our export. Can someone sanity-check before I reply? Link: drive.redwood/vendor/metermate/renewal-draft (redacted)

Owen (ML Eng): I can look — suspicion is that their agent double-counted batched embedding requests as individual calls. We changed client-side batching in Feb.

Tess (Platform): We rolled the SDK that groups 10 embeddings into 1 call on 2026-02-09. If MeterMate's side still counts per-embedding rather than per-call that explains it.

Dara (FinOps): Good catch. Nakul from MeterMate, can you confirm how your collector attributes batched embeddings vs single requests?

Nakul (MeterMate): Hi all ":wave:" — our collector attributes usage by request_id by default; if batching preserves request_id it's counted once, otherwise per-item. Could you share an example request_id and a sample payload?

Owen (ML Eng): Example request id: req_2a9b3f. Payload snippet:```{ "requests": [{"input":"..."},{"input":"..."}, ...] }``` The SDK wraps multiple inputs under one request id.

Nakul (MeterMate): Thanks — I'll pull logs for req_2a9b3f. Quick note: some customers had older SDKs that sent each input as separate request_id; we recently tightened parsing which may change historical reconciliation.

BillingBot: Billing export: /billing/exports/metermate-match-2026-02.csv 

Dara (FinOps): Nakul, for renewal we need two things in the pro-forma: (A) line-by-line reconciliation showing their counted units vs our billing exports for Jan-Mar; (B) a renewal price option that supports batching — e.g., per-call price + per-embed add-on. Also include a credit for INV-2026-0520 if reconciliation shows overcounting.

Priya (Legal): Also ask MeterMate to add an audit clause that allows us to reconcile raw collector logs quarterly for any billed discrepancy >1%. Need wording for the SOW.

Nakul (MeterMate): Understood. I'll produce a CSV mapping request_id -> meter_count -> our_tokens -> their_units, plus two pricing variants: (1) current per-embed model with a retrospective credit if overcounted, (2) per-call base with per-embed delta (better for high batching). Will include SOW audit language draft.

Owen (ML Eng): For the reconciliation, prefer a small query we can run locally to confirm. I usually run:```SELECT request_id, count(*) as items, sum(tokens) FROM api.requests WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-03-31' GROUP BY request_id;```

Dara (FinOps): Good. Nakul can you also give an ETA? We need to close renewal decisions by 2026-04-15.

Nakul (MeterMate): I'll upload pro-forma + reconciliation file in 24 hours. Regarding INV-0520 credit, if overcounting is confirmed we'll apply a one-time credit equal to the overbilled amount or offer a discount on the next invoice — your choice.

Tess (Platform): If we move to per-call + per-embed delta, please model cost with our March traffic and a 15% batching efficiency assumption. That helps procurement.

Dara (FinOps): Also request a short pilot price for 3 months (trial commit) so we can test new meter semantics without full renewal risk. Include the pilot in the quote options.

Priya (Legal): Keep the pilot cancellable with a 30-day notice and no hidden minimums. I'll draft the clause once MeterMate posts their SOW language.

BillingBot: Reminder set: metermate-renewal-decision 2026-04-15 10:00 PT

Nakul (MeterMate): Uploading files now. Linking: /vendor/metermate/recon_1819000246.csv and /vendor/metermate/renewal_proforma_1819000246.csv

Owen (ML Eng): I'll run the reconciliation tonight and paste a quick summary.

Dara (FinOps): Thanks everyone. If the reconciliation shows <1% diff we accept current terms; if >1% we want the credit + pilot option. Tag me with the result. :thumbsup:
